headline: Power Stocks Surge as Chips Lead a Broadly Higher Thursday
body_html:
Equities closed out Thursday's session on firm footing, with 329 of 545 names in our universe finishing in positive territory. The dominant theme was electrification and power demand: semiconductor names led all sectors with a gain of 3.47%, while power-adjacent industrials and homebuilders — up 1.01% — provided meaningful secondary support. Geopolitical tensions surrounding Iran and the broader Middle East, underscored by diplomatic maneuvering at the United Nations ahead of next week's General Assembly, kept energy markets uncertain, though the Energy sector managed a thin 0.09% advance. Consumer names were the lone sector in the red, off 0.03%.

The standout mover of the day was Generac, which surged 18.34% — the strongest single-stock performance across the universe. Vicor Corporation was close behind at 17.66%, reinforcing a clear market bid for companies tied to power generation and delivery infrastructure. Forgent Power Solutions and Arm Holdings also posted strong advances of 9.24% and 8.57%, respectively, rounding out a cohesive theme around energy-intensive computing and grid resilience.

On the other side of the ledger, infrastructure contractor MasTec shed 7.92%, the sharpest single-day loss in the universe. Healthcare devices names STAAR Surgical and Artivion also retreated notably. Thursday's session offered a telling snapshot: capital is rotating toward power generation and chip architecture, and away from construction execution and medical devices.

briefs.headline: Generac Vaults 18% on Power-Demand Conviction
briefs.body: Generac posted the session's largest gain at 18.34%, reflecting intensifying investor conviction that resilient, distributed power generation remains a structural growth story. The move extended a broader theme that also lifted Vicor Corporation and Forgent Power Solutions sharply higher on the same day.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Sector Paces the Market with 3.47% Advance
briefs.body: Chips were the clear sector leader Thursday, gaining 3.47% on average. Arm Holdings added 8.57% and United Microelectronics climbed 8.61%, suggesting the market is rewarding both semiconductor intellectual property and foundry capacity as AI-related power and compute demand continues to expand.

briefs.headline: MasTec Drops Nearly 8% to Pace All Decliners
briefs.body: Infrastructure contractor MasTec fell 7.92%, the steepest single-session loss in our universe on Thursday. The move stood in contrast to the day's broader industrial gains, pointing to stock-specific or contract-related concerns rather than a sector-wide pullback.

briefs.headline: Iran Tensions Color Diplomatic Calendar Ahead of UN General Assembly
briefs.body: World leaders are set to converge on New York for the United Nations General Assembly next week against a complex geopolitical backdrop. Ongoing conflict involving Iran, questions about Houthi influence in Yemen, and debates over independent UN sanctions monitoring kept international headlines heavy, adding an undercurrent of uncertainty to energy markets.

briefs.headline: Vital Farms Jumps 16.65% in Premium Food Breakout
briefs.body: Shares of Vital Farms surged 16.65%, an unusual top-three finish for a consumer staples name on a day when the broader Consumer sector edged fractionally lower. The move underscored that selective premium food brands can decouple sharply from their sector when company-specific momentum takes hold.

briefs.headline: Stocks Recover After Recent Fed-Driven Pressure
briefs.body: Thursday's advance came as equities recouped ground lost in the wake of earlier Federal Reserve-driven volatility. Positive breadth — with advances outnumbering declines by more than 50% — suggested the rebound had meaningful participation, rather than being concentrated solely in a handful of large-cap names.
